boardEligibilityNotice: This independent course gives no board eligibility. Rules change and candidates must confirm with their board. Spaulding lists FM, IM, osteopathic neuromusculoskeletal medicine, pediatrics, and PM&R residencies for this fellowship; Emergency Medicine applicants are directed to a distinct Emergency Sports Medicine Fellowship. Board eligibility requires applicable primary certification, licensure, and completion/verification of accredited fellowship training; independent videos are not a substitute.

boardNames: American Board of Preventive Medicine (ABPM) — Addiction Medicine subspecialty certification examination
American Osteopathic Board of Preventive Medicine (AOBPM) — Addiction Medicine certification (separate osteopathic board pathway; verify current eligibility and exam requirements directly)
boardStatus: Addiction Medicine is a physician subspecialty with a separately administered ABPM subspecialty certification exam (200 questions; four one-hour blocks; 4.5 hours including tutorial and break). ABPM ACGME-fellowship pathway requires at least 12 months in an ACGME-accredited Addiction Medicine fellowship and completion of all accredited years if longer; also requires qualifying medical degree, unrestricted current license, and current primary specialty certification. ACGME programme completion is not itself board certification. AOBPM also lists an osteopathic certification pathway; no equivalence or individual eligibility is implied. AOBPM/American Osteopathic Conjoint Examination Committee separately administers an osteopathic subspecialty certification exam; its public process page lists fellowship-completion and clinical-pathway eligibility routes subject to current board policies.
boardEligibilityNotice: This course does not establish eligibility. ABPM requirements apply to individual applicants, including current primary specialty certification, qualifying medical degree and unrestricted license; only the board determines eligibility. Verify current ABPM/AOBPM rules and application cycle. No promise of exam readiness or passing.
